items.title: The Iran War Shows How Reliant Indian Airlines Are on Gulf Hubs
items.summary: India’s global aviation ambitions still run through the Gulf. When that works, it connects Indian travelers to the world. When geopolitics disrupts it, the shock quickly reaches India’s airlines.

items.title: Hilton’s CEO on Why the Fundamentals Still Win in the AI Era
items.summary: As AI models increasingly decide who gets recommended, Chris Nassetta's view is that the inputs still hold. Reliability, culture, and a lifetime relationship with the guest keep earning the recommendation, even as who does the recommending has changed.

items.title: Expedia Cuts Eight Executives as It Reorganizes Around AI
items.summary: Expedia Group is shedding several senior leaders and shifting others around to reshape leadership and work structure. The goal: To help product and technology efforts move faster.

items.title: Travelodge CEO Exits After Mishandling of Guest’s Sexual Assault Case
items.summary: Boydell’s departure won’t close the book on Travelodge’s security crisis. An independent review is ongoing and industry-wide safety talks have put the sector on notice.

items.title: The Next Dollar: Three Competing Strategies at Lindblad, Intrepid, and Travelopia
items.summary: Lindblad is buying out founders, Travelopia is pruning an asset-heavy portfolio, and Intrepid is buying brands to strengthen its ground network. Each of these companies is deciding which parts of the trip it must control.

items.title: Taj Starts Bringing Staff Back to Dubai Hotels, Others Cautious on Q4 Recovery
items.summary: Dubai’s occupancy rebound is partly a supply story, not a demand one — hotels are using the war to do renovations they needed anyway.

items.title: The UK’s Hidden-Fee Crackdown Is Coming for Travel
items.summary: An investigation isn't a verdict, but the UK regulator no longer needs a court to reach one, and it can fine a company up to 10% of global turnover once it does. The travel industry will be watching very closely.

items.title: Delta’s Texas Ambitions: Is Austin Its Next Hub?
items.summary: Texas is one of the fastest growing states in the U.S., and American, Southwest, and United all have a major presence in the state. Now, Delta is looking to cash in with more growth out of Austin and San Antonio.
